credit.credit-words: Gymnopédie No. 1 for Flute & Easy Piano
(for Flute or other monophonic C instrument)
Erik Satie
(Arranged by dddiam)
Only one voice per staff.
Single-note left hand – no ledger lines.
Simple chords for right hand:
- 3 notes maximum
- at most one ledger line
- inversions designed to minimize finger stretch.
Use of 8vb clefs for easier reading.
Positioning of performer one octave to the left,
rather than in front of Middle C key,
for normal feel of finger positioning
relative to the staffs / clefs.
Simplified jump notation -- No codas.
A single repeat with volta brackets.
Minimal dynamics notation (which may be ignored).
Design for the Easy Piano arrangement:
The flute part is naturally fairly easy.

direction-type.words: *(This is a beuatiful, haunting melody; I prefer "soulful" to Satie's "painful")
Piano is background, supporting the flute.
(Note: Special clefs with an "8" under them mean to play notes an octave lower than written.
Instead of sitting in front of the Middle C key, sit in front of the C key an octave below that).
Chords should be played softer than bass notes, with a hint of a rolled leading edge.
